findings.repair: Resolve with Path(file_path).resolve().relative_to(project_root.resolve()) in a separate hardening change. Out of scope for this packet; not worsened by it.
findings.summary: _repo_relative() is purely lexical: it never resolves '..' segments, and an absolute path outside project_root is used verbatim after a ValueError. A crafted path like '<root>/x/../.github/workflows/ci-complete.yml' yields a relative string no ^-anchored FORBIDDEN_PATHS pattern matches, evading every path-level rule, not just the workflows carve-out.

findings.repair: Introduce a shared path-normalization helper used by both the hook and the scanner. Separate change.
findings.summary: FORBIDDEN_PATHS is matched against raw, unnormalized changed_files strings. './'-prefixed, absolute, or doubled-separator forms can evade path findings (fail-open for evasion in the general case). For the two carved-out files specifically, the doubled-separator form over-blocks (fail-safe), not under-blocks.

Python's '$' anchor matches immediately before a trailing newline, so the literal string 'embedded-audit.yml\n' would technically evade the new negative-lookahead pattern. That string names a distinct filename (containing a newline byte), never the real protected file, so this is not a realistic bypass of the two carved-out files.

findings.repair: Add explicit regression tests for these edge classes alongside the existing hostile-path tests.
findings.summary: No committed test pins case-variant, '..'-traversal, leading-'./', doubled-separator, or trailing-whitespace path inputs against the new carve-out. Behavior for these was verified by direct regex/pathlib reasoning only, and in every case reasoned to be fail-safe (over-blocking), not fail-open.
